laws.rule: A four-wheel drive and a vehicle access permit are needed on Flinders Beach and Main Beach (Minjerribah Recreation Area). No beach access or driving from one hour before to one hour after high tide (80 minutes earlier than Brisbane Bar). Road rules apply on beaches and tracks; speed limits 40 km/h on Flinders Beach, 60 km/h on Main Beach. No driving or parking within one metre of a dune or on dune vegetation.

Camping is not permitted in Naree Budjong Djara National Park. Former mining leases under rehabilitation can't be crossed without prior permission. The southern end, including Stingaree Island and the lands next to Swan Bay, is a restricted access area with no public access on land.
Domestic animals are not permitted in the national park, to protect wildlife including the island's genetically distinct koalas. Go slow and around shorebird flocks on beaches.

culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Kaboora is of special cultural significance: please don't swim in the lake. Eighteen Mile Swamp, midden and bora ring sites, and Moongalba (Myora) Mission and springs are also places of cultural significance. Respect the restricted access area around Swan Bay and Stingaree Island.

laws.rule: Passenger and vehicle ferries run from Toondah Harbour, Cleveland, to Dunwich (passenger about 25 minutes, vehicle about 45). Council lists the operators; book the vehicle ferry directly with the operator. Check that a hire car may travel to the island.

Residents who reasonably need a vehicle access permit to reach their home through the Minjerribah Recreation Area can apply for a fee exemption, with evidence, each year (Recreation Areas Management Regulation 2017 s58). Traditional Owners exercising native title rights are exempt from the fee; for Minjerribah, First Nations applicants need endorsement from the prescribed body corporate first. Renew before it lapses if you will be away at renewal time.
